newsitem.title: USA: USDA again approves New England dairy price plan.
newsitem.headline: USDA again approves New England dairy price plan.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, acting under court scrutiny, again approved on Thursday the creation of the Northeast Dairy Compact.
The compact, already endorsed by the six New England states, allows a regional commission to increase prices of milk bound for retail sale by as much as 25 percent above federal ceilings.

In a five-page "decision" sent to U.S. district court, Glickman said, for the second time, "there is a compelling public interest in the compact region and (I) authorize implementation of the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact."
Glickman again said he held the power to revoke his approval if the commission abused its powers. Revokation is an issue in the court proceedings.

The Milk Industry Foundation sued USDA over its approval. A federal judge has indicated that Congress acted within the Constitution in authorizing the compact but was skeptical USDA did a good enough job of assessing need for it.
In his statement, Glickman said the compact would help preserve small dairy farms. But he said he wanted to make sure that it did not harm low-income families.
Dairy industry groups say the compact will be a cartel that blocks shipment of milk from other regions and will spur other regional blocs to form.

Congress said the compact would have a lifespan of no more than three years and would go out of business after USDA carried out a reform of milk marketing orders, which are regional agreements that help determine the price of milk bound for retail sale.
